newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Rep. Kaptur, Cargill to speak at CBOT hearing.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Rep. Kaptur, Cargill to speak at CBOT hearing.

text.p: Rep. Marcy Kaptur (D-OH) and grain giant Cargill Inc are among 15 participants in an upcoming public hearing by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) on delivery terms, the agency said Monday.

CFTC is holding a rare public hearing on June 12 on the Chicago Board of Trade's controversial proposal to change delivery terms of its corn and soybean futures contracts, which would eliminate the ports of Toledo and St. Louis in favor of the northern Illinois River.
The CFTC said there would be three panels for the three hour hearing, which is slated to begin at 1400 EDT/1800 GMT. Kaptur and Rep. Nick Smith (R-Mich.) are listed as the first panel.
Officials from the Michigan and Ohio agriculture departments and the U.S. Agriculture Department's licensing authority branch will speak in the second panel, CFTC said.

The third panel will be made up of representatives from the Chicago Board of Trade, Cargill, Archer Daniels Midland Co, Andersons Inc, Continental Grain Co, Countymark, Guthrie Corp, the National Corn Growers Association, the American Soybean Association and the American Farm Bureau, CFTC said.
Last week, CFTC head Brooksley Born told reporters the agency would move swiftly to finalize delivery changes after the hearing.

Ohio lawmakers and a host of local farm groups have rallied to demand Toledo remain a delivery site for the two huge CBOT contracts, saying the change would hurt the port and the economy of the city on Lake Erie.
